summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- For more than three decades, international aid has been an indispensable lifeline for Somalia. It has helped prevent humanitarian collapse, funded essential health and education services, and sustained civil-society organizations through cycles of conflict, drought, and displacement. title: From Military Victory to Political Settlement - Why Ethiopia's Real Test Lies Beyond Controlling Mekelle
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Mekelle, the capital of Tigray Regional State, has now changed hands three times in six years. Federal forces took the city in November 2020, within a month of the last war beginning; Tigrayan forces retook it in June 2021. On 3 October 2026, federal troops and the allied Tigray Peace Force entered it again, after the TPLF announced that it had withdrawn and that its regional administration would "temporarily move out" of the capital. title: Ethiopia Warns Somaliland Recognition Could Strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland Officials Push Back
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has warned that recognizing Somaliland could undermine regional counterterrorism efforts and strengthen Al-Shabaab, while Somaliland officials have rejected the security concerns, arguing that recognition would instead enhance regional stability and advance Ethiopia's economic and strategic interests.

title: Oromo Intellectuals Back Ola-Fano Membership in New Armed Alliance, Call for Inclusive Transition in Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A group of Oromo intellectuals and public figures has backed the Oromo Liberation Army's (OLA) participation in a newly formed opposition coalition that includes the Amhara Fano movement, describing the alliance as a potential opening to address Ethiopia's deepening political crisis while calling for an inclusive transition that safeguards the rights and political aspirations of all communities.

title: Airbus Projects Sixfold Growth in Ethiopia's Air Passenger Traffic Over Next 20 Years
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Airbus has forecast a sixfold rise in Ethiopia's air passenger traffic over the next 20 years, saying Ethiopian Airlines is well placed to turn Addis Ababa into one of Africa's leading aviation hubs.

title: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ghana is projected to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to reach US$128.64 billion, exceeding Ethiopia's projected US$127.15 billion by US$1.49 billion, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), as reported by African Business Insider on 17 October.

title: Alliance for Survival Rejects Rubio's Characterization of Ethiopia's Conflict As Separatist, Terrorist
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival (Alliance for Survival), a coalition of armed and political groups opposing the federal government, has rejected remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterizing aspects of Ethiopia's conflict as separatist and terrorist, calling on Washington to adopt what it described as a balanced approach to the conflict.

title: Ugandans in Ethiopia Called to Contribute to Country's Growth Through Investment, Trade and Skills Transfer
summary: [Independent (Kampala)] Addis Ababa -- Uganda convened its diaspora community in Ethiopia for a two-day event at the Hilton Addis Ababa, centered on "Connecting, Celebrating and Contributing: Harnessing the Ugandan Diaspora for National Development." The forum aimed to strengthen ties between Ugandans living in Ethiopia and national development priorities, while showcasing Uganda's culture, investment opportunities, and talent to a global audience.

title: Ethiopia, U.S. Treasury Reaffirm Partnership to Deepen Economic Reforms and Bilateral Engagement
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Ethiopian high-level delegation met with Eric Meyer, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Africa and the Middle East at the U.S. Department of the Treasury, on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

title: African Diplomats Urge Stronger African-Led Strategies, Sustained Dialogue, Local Ownership, Adequate Financing
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- African diplomats have called for stronger African-led strategies to address the continent's conflicts and security challenges.

title: TPLF Warns Against Movement Around Tigray Airports, Rejects Caretaker Administration
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) has warned residents against movement around airports in Tigray, alleging that the Ethiopian federal government is using aviation facilities for military purposes, while rejecting the newly established caretaker administration as illegitimate.

title: Kenya Overtakes Ethiopia As East Africa's Largest Economy in Dollar Terms, IMF Estimates Show
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Kenya has overtaken Ethiopia as Eastern Africa's largest economy measured by nominal gross domestic product (GDP) in US dollar terms, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), a shift largely attributed to exchange-rate movements rather than faster real economic growth.

title: Eritrea Asks AU to Restore Representation After Ethiopia Expels Diplomats
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Eritrea has urged the African Union (AU) to take urgent measures to restore its representation at the organization's headquarters in Addis Abeba, saying Ethiopia's expulsion of 10 Eritrean diplomats has effectively deprived the country of its rights to participate in the continental body's activities.

title: Ethiopia Navy Expanding 'Robust Capabilities' to Neutralize Threats, Safeguard 'National Interests': Vice Admiral
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's Navy is expanding its training capacity, infrastructure and specialized combat units as it seeks to protect "national interests and address security threats", Navy Commander-in-Chief Vice Admiral Kindu Gezu said in an interview with a state-owned media.

title: Why Ethiopia's Return to Red Sea Is Indispensable Asset for Regional Peace and Stability?
summary: [ENA] Ethiopia has a long history of contributing to regional, continental and international peacekeeping missions, guided by its commitment to collective security, Pan-Africanism and regional stability. Its pursuit of reliable maritime access presents an opportunity to expand this role by contributing to maritime security, protecting international trade and promoting lasting peace across the Red Sea region.

title: Ethiopia Reaffirms Commitment to Turning Development Financing Into Jobs
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has reaffirmed its commitment to accelerating development financing and translating investments into tangible economic opportunities, with job creation, poverty reduction, and sustainable growth among its key priorities.

summary: [Reporter] New admin tasked with restoring security, rebuilding institutions and preparing for elections

title: Ethiopia Eyes Bigger Role in Africa's Investment, Financial Markets - House Speaker
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is positioning itself as an increasingly important investment destination and financial market in Africa, driven by economic reforms and expanding cross-border investment partnerships, Speaker of the House of People's Representatives Ahmed Shide said.

title: Ethiopia's New Political Chapter - Sovereign Sea Access At the Heart of National Ambition
summary: [ENA] Ethiopia's new five-year political chapter opens with a defining national ambition: building a peaceful, democratic and prosperous state while pursuing sovereign access to the sea. Under the Medemer Government, the government is highly anticipated to translating its electoral mandate into tangible improvements in citizens' lives while strengthening Ethiopia's strategic position in the Horn of Africa.

title: Ethiopia Seeking Renewable Energy Investment, Stronger Public-Private Partnerships
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is seeking increased investment and stronger public-private partnerships to expand renewable energy use and support agricultural productivity, business growth and improved livelihoods.

title: Egyptian Analyst Rebukes Egypt's Leaders for Trying to Block Ethiopia's Sovereign Right to Red Sea
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Egyptian political analyst Magdi Khalil has strongly criticized the leaders of Egypt for opposing and fighting Ethiopia's right of access to the Red Sea.

title: Somaliland President Rejects Interference Threatening Ethiopia's Security
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Hargeisa -- Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi said on Thursday that Somaliland strongly opposed interference and any actions that could threaten neighbouring Ethiopia's stability and security.

title: Can Ethiopia Ever Be At Peace? Four Reasons Conflict Keeps Flaring Up
summary: [The Conversation Africa] Ethiopia has experienced recurrent conflicts for over five decades. This includes a long-running civil war sparked by the overthrow of Emperor Haile Selassie in 1974, renewed fighting in Tigray, and ongoing conflicts in Amhara and Oromia.

title: Renewed Conflict in Tigray Raises Fears of a New Humanitarian Emergency
summary: [Agenzia Fides] Adigrat -- Nearly a month has passed since fighting resumed in Ethiopia, where an alliance of rebel groups led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) has launched a new offensive, reigniting a conflict that claimed hundreds of thousands of lives between 2020 and 2022.

title: Ethiopia Secures Additional U.S.$8.5 Million in UN Humanitarian Funding
summary: [Reporter] Ethiopia has secured an additional USD8.5 million in United Nations humanitarian funding to provide emergency assistance and protect civilians, with more than 202,700 people expected to benefit across regions facing acute humanitarian needs.

title: IMF Postpones Ethiopia Review Schedule, Board Decision Slated for Early 2027
summary: [Reporter] The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has scheduled discussions on Ethiopia's sixth review under its Extended Credit Facility (ECF) arrangement for November, with a final decision from the Fund's Executive Board expected in early 2027. The schedule pushes the process beyond the previously indicated October 15 milestone.

title: Somaliland, Ethiopia Discuss Defence Cooperation, Regional Development
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Hargeisa -- Somaliland's army chief has met Ethiopian diplomatic and defence officials to discuss strengthening military cooperation and addressing regional security concerns, according to a statement posted on the Somaliland National Army's official social media account.
